leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single prize part on B045 (GLP-1 physiology and incretin therapies) with the same three laureates, Daniel J. Drucker, Jens Juul Holst and Svetlana Mojsov. What is shared: the scientific chain from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect through the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide to drugs with large randomized outcome-trial support, and the judgment that maturity is not in doubt. What is not shared: confidence in the third name. Several members describe Mojsov over Knudsen as a judgment call rather than a settled fact, and the citation wordings differ slightly (for example, whether the discovery is framed as physiology and the active peptide, or as the basis for therapy). Member alternatives are B016 and B007 in every file, in differing order (B016 first for El Manira, Linnarsson, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius; B007 first for Perlmann and Sandberg).

areas_of_agreement: B045 is the sole preferred configuration of all six members, with an identical laureate trio (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov).

Members state that the case rests on mechanism, independent confirmation over about three decades and large randomized cardiovascular, renal and weight outcome trials, not on the opening vote count; maturity of B045 is not disputed in any file.
Every member names B016 (CAR-T) and B007 (unfolded protein response) as the only alternatives, and no member lists any other ballot as an alternative.
Every member names the same weak point in B045: Habener is not among the credited names, the Mojsov-Habener-Holst priority history is contested, and the three-laureate cap excludes Knudsen.
Members treat B007 (Walter, Mori) as a clean two-person attribution and a fundamental advance, with disease relevance described as still largely preclinical or correlative.
scientific_disputes: Whether the prizeworthy achievement is the physiology and peptide biology of GLP-1 (the discovery) or the long-acting analogue drugs that reached patients; members differ in how heavily they weigh this, though all six prefer the discovery trio.

Whether B007 has enough demonstrated disease relevance to stand beside or ahead of B045; Perlmann ranked it first at opening and now keeps it as an alternative, while El Manira, Sandberg, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius and Svenningsson describe its medical payoff as indirect or preclinical.

Whether optogenetics (B004) and antisense correction of SMN2 (B035) deserve a place in a configuration; members who discuss them describe the clinical benefit of B004 as still small and the benefit of B035 as limited to a rare disease, and neither is a listed alternative.
Whether the unfolded protein response is a complete discovery when PERK, ATF6 and the work of Ron and Kaufman fall outside the credited names (Perlmann, Sandberg).
attribution_disputes: B045 third laureate: Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide) versus Knudsen (acylated long-acting analogues). All six configurations list Mojsov; Wahren-Herlenius and Perlmann say excluding Knudsen is uncomfortable, and Wahren-Herlenius would address it in the citation wording.

B045 priority: Habener's contribution to the active peptide is not on the credited list, and no member claims to have audited the Mojsov, Habener and Holst priority record; El Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius each flag it as unresolved.

B016 (CAR-T): the credited trio is June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, but members note that Rosenberg's adoptive transfer and TIL work is adjacent to CAR design and that Eshhar, an original CAR pioneer, is not credited; Sandberg and Svenningsson see a two-person June-Sadelain credit as more fragile than the three-name version.
B004 (optogenetics): any three of the six credited names exclude Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenböck, and members state they cannot justify the exclusions on scientific grounds.
B035 (SMA antisense): the SMN1 gene discoverers (Melki, Lefebvre, Dreyfuss) are not on the ballot, so the discovery chain is partly incomplete.
maturity_disputes: No member disputes the maturity of B045; the explicit maturity question concerns B007, whose disease-relevant evidence several members describe as not yet at the level of incretin therapy.
Members describe clinical use of optogenetics (B004) as early, and Linnarsson, Sandberg and Svenningsson place it behind B045, B016 and B007 this year.
Perlmann is uneasy rewarding a single antisense drug (B035) before the Committee has decided how to treat RNA therapeutics as a whole.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Perlmann and Svenningsson both disclose roughly twenty co-authored works with each other (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy); both state that no shortlisted credited name is involved and neither files a recusal.
El Manira discloses a 2009 co-authored paper with Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons; no credited name is involved.
Sandberg discloses co-authorship with committee colleagues (Linnarsson, Frisén); no credited name is involved.
Svenningsson discloses having worked with Paul Greengard, who is not credited on any shortlisted ballot, and notes only a field-level link to B004 and B035.
No member reports a conflict with any credited name on the shortlist, and no member requests recusal.
questions_for_round2: Given the three-laureate cap, should the third B045 place go to Mojsov or Knudsen, and should that rest on the discovery-versus-development principle or on what the attribution review shows about Mojsov's priority over Habener and Holst?
If Mojsov is retained, can the citation wording acknowledge long-acting analogue development without implying a fourth laureate, and what exact wording would members accept?
Is B045 alone a sufficient single-part prize, or should the Committee pair it with a second part, and if so is B016 or B007 the better second part?
If B016 is considered, can June and Sadelain alone be defended given Rosenberg's adjacent contribution and Eshhar's absence from the credited names, or is the Rosenberg inclusion necessary?
If B007 is considered, what disease-relevant evidence would members need to see, and does the omission of PERK, ATF6, Ron and Kaufman from the credited names weaken a Walter and Mori prize?
Does any member wish to move B004 or B035 into a preferred configuration, and if so how would the exclusions of Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenböck or the SMN1 discoverers be handled?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows complete convergence on the B045 trio of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, with B016 and B007 as the only alternatives. The remaining disagreement is not about B045's merit or maturity but about the third name, the unresolved Habener priority question, and whether a second prize part is warranted. Members repeatedly caution that opening-round agreement does not substitute for an attribution review that nobody has yet audited.
